text.text_excerpt: A friend asked if I would like to join her for lunch at Milkfish on Carrollton. I'm so pleased that MidCity is getting a more diverse range of restaurants, and I had heard great things about Milkfish from the other Elites since their UYE, when Milkfish was still a pop-up. There's a narrow hall with some beautiful ink and watercolor artwork, and then you turn into their dining room with a primary color scheme and more great paintings. We were early lunch goers so we basically had the dining room to ourselves for most of the lunch with a bunch of seats filling up on our way out. I'm not familiar with Filipino food at all, but I'm definitely a new fan! You have to have the ceviche. For yours...

Having spent a month in the Philippines, I was excited to try Milkfish. Their new location is wonderfully accessible. The seating is intimate and the service is great. Food-wise: - The regular lumpia could have been rolled and fried a bit better (ex. lacked some stuffing to make it hearty and was burnt on one end for all of them we were served), but the taste was good. It also sounds like they've went from 2x rolls cut in half to 3x for the $7, which is nice. Overall, it was a good starter. - Pork adobo was a huge portion for the price. It's not a recipe that I'm used to, but the flavor was good and my friend finished the entire portion. So it must have been good. Sorry, I'm still loyal t...

Milkfish introduced me filipino food, and I've never looked back since then. There's no other cuisine with all of the flavors that can be found in filipino cuisine. While everything at this restaurant is amazing, my personal favorites are the lumpia (think of them as skinny egg rolls, with more meat), the bagoong fried rice (tangy flavors in this are the jam), and the kare kare (oxtail curry). The servers are fantastic, and the chef is always kind and welcomes talking to the customers, and sharing more about her food and background. Definitely a favorite of mine in NOLA.
